Definition: a primary preposition; "fore", i.e. in front of, prior (figuratively, superior) to:--above, ago, before, or ever. In the compounds, it retains the same significations.
BiblicalUsage: Pro means before, in front of, prior to, and it opens the door to foreordination. Paul says the wisdom of God was ordained before the world, and Peter says Christ was foreordained before the foundation of the world.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that nothing about my salvation is an afterthought, because God settled it before the world began.
